drafted_from: tool:blur-faces-not-agreed's own row in tools/media-composition/tool-rows.json, tools/media-composition/do-work/blur-faces-not-agreed.py (its docstring and the line it prints), and its re-encode run here on a synthetic 3 second test pattern with no faces and no sound; the face and voice models are not on this computer so the detector itself was not run
start_here: Say to your AI: "Make a copy of my practice video with everyone blurred and silenced except the people who agreed to be filmed." It runs tool:blur-faces-not-agreed and keeps the copy in your files.
no_lists_because: It reads the video and the agreed pictures and voices you name and keeps one copy of the video, so it keeps no list of its own.
instructions: 1. Find the video's identity in your files, a clear picture of each person who agreed to be filmed (yourself included) and, for the sound, a recording of each of them speaking for ten seconds or more.

2. Say "Blur everyone who has not agreed" with video, agreed (the pictures) and agreed_voices (the recordings), and name for what to call the copy. With no agreed pictures every face is blurred; with no agreed voices every word is silenced. Raise match or voice_match to blur or silence more.

3. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run and tool tool:blur-faces-not-agreed. It runs on the tool's own computer with no network. The door runs it in a container and answers {"result": {...}}; an error comes back as {"error": "what to change"}.

4. Read result: faces seen, blurred, kept, agreed_faces, pictures_without_a_face (an agreed picture where no face was found: replace it), silenced and silenced_seconds. The copy is files.video, kept under Made by tools; the original is never changed.

worked_examples.title: No one agreed: every face would be blurred
worked_examples.ask: Make a copy of my street practice video with every face blurred.
worked_examples.given: read from tools/media-composition/do-work/blur-faces-not-agreed.py on a 3 second 320x180 clip at 10 frames a second with no sound and no face in the picture: frames 30 and seconds 3.0 come from the probe, every count is 0, and video_bytes is the size of the same ffmpeg re-encode run here (the container's ffmpeg may differ by a few bytes)
